L0_MLP.hypothesis: L0_MLP detects parity of each token independently, writing a binary signal (positive direction for even, negative for odd) from a single source (token at its position).

L1H0_ATTN.hypothesis: L1H0_ATTN routes content from the odd token's position to all other positions via perfect concentration of attention (1.0) on the odd position when one exists, acting as index-based content copying.

L1_MLP.hypothesis: L1_MLP fuses two distinct upstream signals—the parity indicator from L0_MLP and the routed odd-token signal from L1H0_ATTN—both ablations causing ~2000-unit changes in its write.

L2_MLP.hypothesis: L2_MLP combines multiple distinct upstream signals (L0_MLP, L1H0_ATTN, L1_MLP all cause large independent write changes) and is essential for correct predictions (ablating it makes all outputs predict 1).
